articles.title: Private IPv4 & NAT
articles.principle: A private IP identifies a device inside a network. NAT lets devices using private addresses communicate through an internet-facing address.
articles.body:
Start with the address

An IPv4 address is four numbers separated by dots, such as 10.0.0.25. Each number can be 0–255. Your laptop needs an address so other devices can send traffic to it. A private address can be reused inside different homes and businesses because it is not routed directly across the public internet.

Private rangeExample
10.0.0.0–10.255.255.25510.0.0.25
172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255172.20.5.10
192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255192.168.1.20

A 10.x address is just as private as a 192.168.x address. The administrator or router configuration chooses which range to use. Only 172.16 through 172.31 is private in the 172 range. Also notice the spelling: 196.168 is different from 192.168. Addresses outside these ranges are not automatically public; other special ranges exist.

What NAT actually changes

Network Address Translation (NAT) changes addresses as traffic passes through a router or firewall. In a typical office, the device changes a laptop’s private source address into the address used on the internet side. Port Address Translation (PAT) also tracks port numbers, allowing many laptops to share one public address. A port identifies a particular service or connection on a device.

Laptop                  Office gateway              Website
10.0.0.25:53010    →     203.0.113.10:62001     →     TCP 443
                        Translation recorded
Reply to :62001   →     matches the record     →     laptop :53010

The gateway keeps a translation table so replies return to the right laptop. The public address above is reserved for documentation. Real connections can also pass through another translation at the internet provider.

Different networks can share an internet connection

An office might put staff in 10.10.10.0/24 and guests in 192.168.20.0/24. Both can use the same public internet address. Creating another VLAN or subnet does not automatically create or require another public IP. Internal separation and internet address translation are separate settings.

Use it on a support or security ticket

If a user reports “my IP is 10.x instead of 192.168.x,” that alone is not a fault. Compare their address, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS servers with the intended network using ipconfig /all. When investigating an external service’s logs, its recorded source may be the office’s public address. Use the timestamp and translation or connection records to identify an internal device; do not assume that public address identifies one employee.

Remember

NAT changes addresses. Firewall rules decide which traffic is allowed. A malicious program can still make outbound connections through NAT.
articles.question: Do a staff VLAN and a guest VLAN need separate public IP addresses?
articles.answer: No. They can use different private subnets and share a public address through PAT. Their separation depends on VLAN configuration and the rules controlling traffic between them, not on having different public IPs.

articles.title: Subnetting
articles.principle: Subnetting divides an IP address range into smaller networks. The subnet mask tells a device which addresses are local and which need a router.
articles.body:
What the slash means

In 192.168.204.30/28, the address identifies a device and /28 describes its network size. IPv4 has 32 bits: 28 identify the network and the remaining 4 distinguish addresses inside it. A bit is one binary digit, 0 or 1. An octet is a group of eight bits: eight bits can represent 256 values, numbered 0–255.

A subnet mask writes those network bits as ones and the host bits as zeros. The /28 mask is 11111111.11111111.11111111.11110000, or 255.255.255.240. For a destination on the same subnet, a host usually communicates directly. For another subnet, it normally sends the packet to its default gateway, a router interface.

Count the addresses

Host bits = 32 − prefix
Total addresses = 2host bits
Ordinary usable addresses = total − 2

For /28: 4 host bits give 16 total addresses. The first is the network address, the label for the whole subnet. The last is the broadcast address, used to address the subnet’s devices collectively. That leaves 14 ordinary host addresses. A gateway uses one of those 14; it is not a bonus address.

Work through 192.168.204.30/28

  1. Find the mask: 255.255.255.240.
  2. Find the increment in the changing octet: 256 − 240 = 16. Fourth-octet blocks start at 0, 16, 32, 48, and so on.
  3. 30 sits in the 16–31 block. Network: 192.168.204.16.
  4. The next block starts at .32, so broadcast is 192.168.204.31.
  5. Usable addresses: 192.168.204.17–192.168.204.30. The original address .30 is the last usable host.
INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Move the network boundary

Change the prefix or enter an address. Predict the network and broadcast before revealing the calculation.

When the boundary is in the third octet

For 10.50.132.75/21, 11 host bits give 2,048 total addresses. The mask is 255.255.248.0. Its third-octet increment is 256 − 248 = 8. The block containing 132 runs from 128 through 135.

ResultAddress
Network10.50.128.0
Broadcast10.50.135.255
Usable range10.50.128.1–10.50.135.254
Ordinary capacity2,046 host addresses

The increment is 8 in the third octet, while the entire subnet contains 2,048 addresses. These are different quantities. Calculate the broadcast from the network boundary, not by adding the increment to the original host address.

Use it at work

For a department with 50 devices, /26 provides 62 ordinary host addresses, leaving room for a gateway and some growth. Subnetting also helps diagnose a wrong mask, an incorrect gateway, or an overly broad firewall rule. An address plan still needs gateways, DHCP settings, and switch configuration to become a working network.

Two exceptions

The “minus two” rule describes ordinary IPv4 broadcast subnets. /31 point-to-point links can use both addresses; /32 identifies one address. Cloud platforms can reserve extra addresses.
articles.question: Find the network, broadcast, mask, and ordinary usable capacity of 172.19.155.200/18.
articles.answer: The mask is 255.255.192.0. The increment is 64 in the third octet, so 155 sits in 128–191. Network: 172.19.128.0. Broadcast: 172.19.191.255. Usable range: 172.19.128.1–172.19.191.254, giving 16,382 addresses.

articles.title: VLSM
articles.principle: Variable Length Subnet Masking gives each subnet a size that fits its needs, instead of giving every department the same-sized block.
articles.body:
Why use different sizes?

Suppose a warehouse needs 100 device addresses but a kiosk network needs only 12. Giving both a /25 would reserve 128 addresses for each. VLSM lets the warehouse use /25 and the kiosks use /28. Both subnets can fit inside a larger allocation without overlapping. Read Subnetting first if network and broadcast addresses are still unfamiliar.

Choose a prefix from a requirement

Choose enough host bits that 2^h − 2 covers the required host addresses. Then calculate 32 − h for the prefix. For 100 devices, /26 gives only 62 usable addresses. /25 gives 126. Count the gateway, printers, management interfaces, and growth before finalizing a real plan.

Devices in this exerciseCandidateOrdinary capacity
100/25126
50/2662
28/2730
12/2814

Allocate the biggest blocks first

Use 10.60.24.0/24 as the parent allocation. Start with the largest requirement and place the next subnet after the previous subnet’s broadcast address. Each start must also be a valid boundary for its prefix.

DepartmentSubnetUsable rangeBroadcast
Warehouse10.60.24.0/25.1–.126.127
Engineering10.60.24.128/26.129–.190.191
Sales10.60.24.192/27.193–.222.223
Kiosks10.60.24.224/28.225–.238.239

All shortened addresses keep the first three octets 10.60.24. The final block, 10.60.24.240/28, remains available. The first child can start at the same address as its parent: /24 describes the whole allocation, while /25 describes only its first half.

Catch the common mistakes

  • A /26 starts at a multiple of 64 in the fourth octet: .0, .64, .128, or .192. “The next free address” is not enough if it is misaligned.
  • The network and broadcast are not ordinary device addresses. In the kiosk subnet, .224 is the network, .239 is the broadcast, and .225–.238 are usable.
  • The prefix is part of the network definition. Write 10.60.24.128/26, not just “.128.”
  • Largest-first allocation is a practical method that avoids fragmentation. It is not a protocol requirement.

Turn the plan into a working office

Create the intended VLANs, assign their switch ports, and configure a router or Layer 3 switch interface for each subnet. Set up DHCP scopes with the matching mask, gateway, and DNS servers. Reserve or exclude statically assigned infrastructure addresses. Then apply rules for permitted traffic between departments and test both an allowed and a blocked connection. The calculation decides address capacity; these configuration steps implement it.
articles.question: Why can’t 50 engineering devices use a /27, and what else should you count before choosing a /26?
articles.answer: A /27 has only 30 ordinary usable addresses. A /26 has 62. Count the gateway, other infrastructure, and expected growth as well as the 50 devices. Ensure the chosen block starts on a valid boundary and does not overlap another subnet.

articles.title: VLANs
articles.principle: A VLAN makes one physical switch behave like several separate local networks. Devices share a local broadcast network only when their ports belong to the same VLAN.
articles.body:
Picture an office switch

A switch connects laptops, printers, and other devices by cable. Without separation, those devices may all share one local network. A Virtual Local Area Network assigns ports to separate groups. Staff can be in VLAN 10, guests in VLAN 20, and servers in VLAN 30, even when they connect to the same switch.

A broadcast is a message sent to every device in a local broadcast domain. For example, an ARP request asks which device owns a particular local IP. The switch floods that broadcast within its VLAN, not into every VLAN. This separation is the basic job of a VLAN.

INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

One switch. Separate networks.

Move the guest laptop between VLANs, then test its path to the server. Watch which boundary needs a routing policy.

Ports, tags, and subnets

TermMeaning
Access portNormally carries one VLAN for an end device. The attached laptop usually sends untagged frames.
Trunk portCarries multiple VLANs between network devices, commonly using 802.1Q tags to identify each VLAN.
SubnetThe IP address range used on a network. A common office design assigns a different subnet to each VLAN.
Inter-VLAN routingA router or Layer 3 switch moves traffic between VLANs. Firewall rules or access control lists can restrict that traffic.

A VLAN and a subnet are different settings. The VLAN is the local Ethernet separation; the subnet tells IP devices what is local. They are normally planned together. Giving a laptop an address from a different subnet does not move its switch port into another VLAN.

What actually protects the server?

If guests and servers are in different VLANs, a guest cannot directly reach the server through ordinary same-VLAN switching. But if a router connects the two networks and allows the traffic, the guest can still reach the server. The intended policy might allow guests to use the internet while denying connections to server addresses.

If an administrator accidentally places a guest port in the server VLAN, traffic may stay inside that VLAN and bypass the inter-VLAN firewall. Check VLAN membership as well as the rules between networks. Hosts and applications also need their own controls.

Use it on a client ticket

  1. Confirm the device’s IP, mask, gateway, and physical switch port.
  2. Check the port’s VLAN and whether the expected VLAN is allowed on upstream trunks.
  3. Check that this VLAN has the right gateway and DHCP scope or relay.
  4. For cross-VLAN access, inspect the route and the rule for the specific source, destination, protocol, and port.
  5. After an approved change, verify the intended connection works and a forbidden connection remains blocked.
Public IPs are separate

Staff and guest VLANs can share the same public IP for internet access. A VLAN creates local separation, not a new internet subscription.
articles.question: A guest VLAN exists, but guests can still open the file server. What would you investigate?
articles.answer: Check that the guest is actually on the guest VLAN, then inspect routing and firewall or ACL rules between guests and servers. Separate VLANs alone do not guarantee a deny policy. Verify the exact service and both allowed and blocked paths.

articles.title: ARP
articles.principle: ARP finds the MAC address needed to deliver IPv4 traffic to the next device on a local network. For a remote destination, that device is usually your gateway.
articles.keywords: address resolution protocol MAC Ethernet broadcast cache next hop gateway spoofing poisoning
articles.body:
Why an IP address is not enough

Your laptop wants to send data to a printer. It knows the printer’s IPv4 address, but an Ethernet network delivers local traffic using MAC addresses. A MAC address identifies a network interface on that link, often written as six hexadecimal pairs, such as 02:00:00:00:00:50. It is different from the IP address and is not a permanent proof of device identity.

An IP packet carries the network-layer destination. For its trip across an Ethernet link, that packet sits inside a frame with local source and destination MAC addresses. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) supplies the missing IPv4-to-MAC mapping for the next hop: the device that should receive this frame.

Ask the local network, then remember the reply

Imagine a laptop at 10.20.10.25/24 and a printer at 10.20.10.50/24, both on the same VLAN.

  1. The laptop checks its routing information. In this simple network, the printer is directly reachable on the local subnet.
  2. It checks its ARP cache, a temporary table of IP-to-MAC mappings. A usable entry can avoid a new request.
  3. Without an entry, it broadcasts an ARP request: “Who has 10.20.10.50? Tell 10.20.10.25.” The Ethernet destination is ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, the broadcast address. The switch distributes it within that VLAN.
  4. The printer normally replies directly to the laptop with its MAC address. The laptop caches the mapping and can address the frame to the printer.

Other devices can hear the request, but they do not normally answer for an address they do not own. ARP itself runs directly over the local link; it does not use a TCP or UDP port.

What changes when the destination is remote?

Now the laptop wants to reach a website outside its subnet. With a default route through 10.20.10.1, it resolves the gateway’s MAC address. It does not broadcast across the internet asking for the website’s MAC.

The frame is addressed to the gateway, while the packet inside still names the website’s IP as its destination. The router removes the incoming link-layer framing and forwards the packet using the next link’s addressing. Ordinary ARP broadcasts do not pass through routers. This is why understanding the subnet and gateway comes before interpreting an ARP lookup.

INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Who should answer?

Choose a printer or a remote website. Follow the lookup, request, reply, and first frame. Send again to see what the cache changes.

Keep the different tables straight

MechanismQuestion it answers
DHCPWhich IP configuration should this device use?
DNSWhat address is associated with this name?
Routing tableWhich next hop and interface should carry this IP packet?
ARP cacheWhich MAC address corresponds to that local IPv4 next hop?
Switch MAC tableWhich switch port leads toward this MAC address in this VLAN?

Use it on a connectivity ticket

A laptop has a valid address but cannot reach the gateway. Check its address, mask, gateway, and VLAN first. On Windows, arp -a displays cached mappings, separated by interface. Compare the relevant next-hop entry with the expected device, and inspect a capture with Wireshark’s arp display filter if needed.

Repeated requests without replies can suggest an offline next hop, wrong VLAN, incorrect addressing, or a filtering/link problem. Check the capture location too. A MAC entry proves neither that the application works nor that its IP owner is authentic. Record evidence before clearing a cache; “delete everything and retry” can hide a useful clue.

Address changes and security

Dynamic entries age or are refreshed according to the operating system. Devices can also announce an address mapping without first receiving an ordinary request, often called gratuitous ARP. ARP probes and announcements support address-conflict detection and legitimate changes such as failover, so a mapping change is not automatically an attack.

ARP does not authenticate ownership of an address. False mappings, called ARP spoofing or cache poisoning, can redirect or disrupt local traffic. Investigate unexpected gateway mappings alongside device and switch evidence. On supported switches, Dynamic ARP Inspection validates ARP information against trusted bindings, commonly learned through DHCP snooping; static devices and trusted ports need appropriate configuration.

Scope to remember

This note describes ordinary IPv4 over Ethernet. Proxy ARP is a special case where a router answers on another device’s behalf. IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery rather than ARP.
articles.question: Your laptop sends to a website outside its /24 subnet. Does ARP look up the website’s MAC address or the default gateway’s, and which IP remains inside the packet?
articles.answer: With the default route selected, ARP resolves the gateway’s local IPv4 address to its MAC. The Ethernet frame goes to that gateway, while the enclosed IP packet still names the website as its destination. A usable cached gateway mapping can avoid a new ARP request.

articles.title: DNS
articles.principle: DNS translates names such as portal.example.com into information computers can use, often an IP address. It helps find a destination; it does not establish the connection.
articles.body:
Why names need a lookup

People remember a name more easily than a server’s IP address. When an application needs an address, your computer checks available cached information and normally asks its configured DNS resolver. The resolver may answer from its cache or ask other DNS servers until it finds the authoritative answer. Authoritative means the server holds the published records for that DNS zone.

Caching saves repeated lookups. A record’s TTL, or time to live, tells a cache how long it may keep that record before checking again. This helps explain why a DNS change can appear to work on one device while another still uses an older answer.

Records you will encounter

RecordWhat it tells you
A / AAAAThe IPv4 / IPv6 address associated with a name.
CNAMEAn alias pointing to another name.
MXWhich mail servers receive email for a domain.
TXTText used for purposes such as domain verification and email authentication policies.
PTRA reverse lookup from an IP address to a name, when configured.
SRVWhere a particular service can be found; Active Directory uses these to locate domain services.

Separate a name problem from a service problem

A user says websites fail, but your remote-support session still works. That proves some connectivity remains. It does not prove DNS is the cause: an existing session might not need a new lookup, and websites may use a different path or policy.

ipconfig /all
nslookup portal.example.com
Resolve-DnsName portal.example.com
Test-NetConnection portal.example.com -Port 443

These Windows checks show the configured DNS servers, query a name, and test the service’s TCP port. Replace the example with the actual affected hostname. Test-NetConnection proves a TCP connection can be established, not that HTTPS or the application is healthy. Browsing to a bare IP can fail because certificates and website routing expect a hostname.

Read the symptom before changing settings

SymptomUseful next check
Name does not exist / NXDOMAINCheck spelling and whether the expected record exists in the correct DNS zone.
Query times outCheck reachability to the configured resolver and whether it answers other queries.
An unexpected address is returnedCompare intended records, caches, split DNS, and recent changes.
Correct address, but application failsCheck the service port, TLS, proxy, firewall, and application health.

Internal names may only exist on company DNS servers, often reachable through an approved remote-access path. Replacing corporate DNS with a public resolver can break domain logons or file-server lookups. Record the query, resolver, answer, and time before clearing a cache; that evidence can explain what happened.
articles.question: A name resolves to the expected IP, but the website still fails. What has DNS proved?
articles.answer: It has provided the expected address for that lookup. It has not proved that the service port is reachable, the TLS handshake works, or the application is healthy. Test those separately and compare the scope of affected users.

articles.title: DHCP
articles.principle: DHCP automatically gives a device an IP address and the network settings it needs. The address is borrowed for a lease period, rather than manually typed into every computer.
articles.body:
What a new laptop needs

When a laptop joins an office network, it needs an available IP address, a subnet mask, a default gateway for reaching other networks, and DNS servers for looking up names. Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol supplies these settings. A home router often runs the DHCP service, but a business may use Windows Server, a firewall, or another network service. DHCP is not limited to routers.

The first lease: DORA

  1. Discover: the client looks for a DHCP server. It does not yet have a usable lease for this network.
  2. Offer: a server offers an address and configuration.
  3. Request: the client requests the selected offer.
  4. Acknowledge: the server confirms the lease. The client can apply the settings after its normal checks.
INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Watch a laptop join the network

Step through the initial IPv4 lease exchange, then try it with the server unavailable.

This is the common initial IPv4 exchange. Renewing an existing lease usually starts with a Request, not a complete Discover/Offer cycle. DHCPv4 uses UDP ports 67 for the server and 68 for the client.

Read a DHCP scope

SettingExample and purpose
ScopeThe address pool and settings for one subnet: 10.20.30.0/24.
PoolOffer 10.20.30.50–10.20.30.200 to clients.
ExclusionKeep statically configured devices out of the offered pool.
ReservationGive a particular client a consistent address through DHCP, commonly identified by its MAC address or client identifier.
LeaseHow long the client may use the assignment before it expires unless renewed.
OptionsSupply the gateway and DNS servers. Option 003 is routers; 006 is DNS servers in common Windows DHCP administration.

A reservation still depends on DHCP. A manually configured static address is set on the device itself. Plan both so two devices are not assigned the same address.

Why VLANs sometimes need a relay

The first broadcast does not normally cross a router. If the DHCP server is on another subnet, a DHCP relay forwards the request and identifies the client’s network so the server can choose the right scope. A new VLAN may have perfectly good switch ports but no functioning DHCP path if its relay or scope is missing.

Troubleshoot “I have no network”

Start with ipconfig /all. Check whether DHCP is enabled, which server supplied the lease, the address, mask, gateway, DNS servers, and lease times. On a Windows client configured for DHCP, an unexpected 169.254.x.x link-local address is a clue that it could not obtain a lease. It is not proof of the exact failure.

Compare another device on the same VLAN. Check scope exhaustion, server health, relay settings, switch VLAN membership, and unexpected DHCP servers. A wrong DNS option can produce a valid IP but broken name lookups. Releasing an address can disconnect a remote-support session, so plan any renewal work around the user’s access.
articles.question: Devices on one new VLAN get 169.254 addresses, while other VLANs work. What would you check?
articles.answer: Confirm the clients are using DHCP and are on the intended VLAN. Check that VLAN’s scope, available addresses, gateway relay, and path to the DHCP server. A failure limited to one VLAN points toward its configuration or path, though the address alone does not prove the cause.

articles.title: Syslog
articles.principle: Syslog is a common way for devices and applications to send event messages to a central place. Instead of opening every firewall or server, an analyst can review their messages together.
articles.body:
Start with one event

A switch port goes down. A firewall blocks a connection. A Linux service fails to start. Each system can write a message describing what happened. With syslog forwarding configured, it also sends that message to a collector: a server that receives logs from other systems.

A log is a recorded event. A collector stores or forwards those events. A SIEM can search and analyze collected events and create alerts using rules. Receiving a syslog message does not automatically mean an attack was detected.

Read the message in pieces

<134>1 2026-09-05T10:15:00Z fw-01 firewall 812 DENY - Blocked TCP from 10.20.10.25 to 10.20.30.10:445

This fictional RFC 5424-style message records one blocked connection. fw-01 identifies the reporting device; the timestamp says when it recorded the event. The final text explains the action, source, and destination. 445 is a service port commonly used for SMB file sharing.

FieldHow to read it
<134>Priority combines a facility and severity. Here 16 × 8 + 6 = 134: local0 facility, informational severity.
1The syslog message format version.
2026-09-05T10:15:00ZEvent time; Z means UTC.
fw-01 / firewall / 812Hostname, application name, and process identifier.
DENY / -Message identifier, then no structured data.
Blocked TCP…The human-readable event description. Vendor message bodies vary.
INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Which messages reach the collector?

Change the forwarding threshold. Lower severity numbers are more urgent; the word “blocked” does not automatically mean “critical.”

Severity is a label, not a verdict

Syslog has eight severity levels: 0 emergency, 1 alert, 2 critical, 3 error, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 informational, and 7 debug. The sender assigns a level. A normal firewall deny can be informational. An informational event can still matter to an investigation. If a device forwards only warning and more urgent messages, levels 5–7 may never reach the collector.

How the messages travel

The device needs a destination collector address, a transport and port, and a choice of messages to forward. Traditional UDP syslog commonly uses port 514. UDP provides no delivery acknowledgement, so messages can be lost. Syslog over TLS commonly uses TCP 6514 to protect the connection. Plain TCP alone does not encrypt the messages; the sender and receiver must support and agree on the chosen transport.

Use it in an investigation

Suppose a user cannot reach a file server. Search the firewall’s collected events for the user’s source IP, the server’s destination IP, port 445, and the time of the attempt. A matching deny can identify the rule that blocked it. Record the rule and intended access before changing it.

If no message appears, check whether the device generated it locally, whether its forwarding filter includes that severity, and whether the collector is receiving other events. Then check parsing, timestamps, and the search time range. “No results” can mean missing collection or a wrong query, not “nothing happened.”
articles.question: A firewall shows a local informational deny event, but the collector only receives warning and more urgent events. Why is your search empty?
articles.answer: Informational is severity 6; warning is 4. A threshold that includes only 0–4 excludes that deny. Check the forwarding filter and collection path before concluding that the event did not happen. The sender’s severity is not an analyst’s final threat assessment.

articles.title: EDR, MDR, and XDR
articles.principle: EDR watches devices. XDR brings signals from several security areas together. MDR provides people and processes to investigate and respond using those tools.
articles.body:
Start with the problem

A user opens an attachment and something suspicious runs on their laptop. You need to know what ran, whether it caused harm, whether other accounts or devices are involved, and who will respond. EDR, XDR, and MDR address different parts of this work. They are not three mutually exclusive products or a required sequence of upgrades.

Understand each role

TermWhat it contributesExample
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR)Software records device activity such as processes, files, and network connections. It can detect threats and perform supported response actions.SentinelOne or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
Extended Detection and Response (XDR)A platform links related signals across areas such as endpoints, email, identities, and cloud applications.Connecting a phishing email, a suspicious process, and a risky account sign-in into an investigation.
Managed Detection and Response (MDR)A service supplies analysts and an agreed process for monitoring, investigation, and response. It uses its own and/or integrated tools.A Blackpoint SOC analyst investigates an integrated SentinelOne alert and takes action within the contracted scope.

An endpoint is a device such as a laptop or server. Telemetry means the recorded activity it sends. A SOC, or security operations center, is the team and function that monitors and responds to threats. MDR adds that operational service; XDR describes a technology approach, not automatically a staffed team.

INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Follow one suspicious attachment

Step through the same fictional incident to see what the endpoint tool, broader platform, and responding people contribute.

How an EDR can feed an MDR service

An endpoint agent sends activity and alerts to its product’s platform. A supported integration can share those alerts and relevant context with an MDR provider, often through an API: a structured connection between products. The provider’s analysts investigate with the available evidence and their own sensors or connected services. Depending on permissions, they may use that integration to stop a process or isolate a device.

For a concrete example, Blackpoint documents a SentinelOne integration that monitors alerts, supports response, and writes resolution information back into SentinelOne. This requires a configured integration and service coverage. It is not a guarantee that every raw endpoint event or firewall log is included in every MDR plan.

Where XDR and a SIEM fit

An XDR platform can connect the endpoint alert to an email delivered to the same person and a suspicious sign-in. A SIEM provides broader log collection, search, and detection across configured sources. Their capabilities can overlap and integrate. Microsoft Sentinel is a separate product from SentinelOne; Sentinel and Defender XDR can share an investigation experience.

What an analyst still needs to do

  • Confirm the customer, affected device, user, timestamp, and evidence behind the alert.
  • Read what automatic response or the MDR provider already completed. “Detected” is different from “successfully contained.”
  • Determine scope: other devices, mailbox activity, account use, and business impact.
  • Follow the response plan. Urgent containment can happen while investigation continues when the evidence and authority justify it.
  • Document actions, owners, outstanding tasks, and the evidence needed before restoring access.
Do not equate the labels

MDR does not simply mean “a place to view firewall logs.” The defining feature is the managed investigation and response service. Verify the actual data sources and responsibilities in the deployed service.
articles.question: Why would an organization use SentinelOne and Blackpoint together instead of choosing only one?
articles.answer: SentinelOne supplies endpoint visibility and response controls. With the supported integration and coverage configured, Blackpoint can provide continuous monitoring, investigation, and response around those alerts and its other evidence. The organization still coordinates business impact, remediation, and follow-up. XDR can add broader correlation across security areas.

articles.title: SentinelOne
articles.principle: SentinelOne’s console lets you inspect protected devices, investigate detections through Storyline, and check or perform response actions on the affected endpoint.
articles.body:
This is a console study guide. For the general security categories, read EDR, MDR, and XDR. SentinelOne is a different product from Microsoft Sentinel. Product screens, labels, available actions, and access depend on the console version, operating system, license, and assigned role.

Find the right place

Area or featureUse it to
Account / Site / Group scopeConfirm which customer and device group you are viewing before investigating or acting.
Endpoints / SentinelsFind a device and inspect its identity, operating system, agent health, last contact, policy, and connectivity.
Alerts / ThreatsReview detections, timestamps, severity, status, and any actions already attempted.
Storyline / ExploreInspect linked activity and the process tree: what launched what, and what each process did.
Deep VisibilitySearch available historical endpoint activity, such as a filename, hash, process, or network destination.
Policy and response controlsReview configured behavior and permitted actions. Verify the selected scope before changing anything.

Work through a detection

  1. Confirm the customer and endpoint. Record the detection ID, time, username, and current status.
  2. Open the detection details. Read the reason it fired and the action results. A failed or pending action needs different follow-up from a completed one.
  3. Inspect Storyline. A process is a running program; its parent is the program that launched it. Read the command line, file path, signature information, and related network activity.
  4. Compare the activity with approved software and change records. PowerShell can be legitimate administration; the command, origin, and behavior matter.
  5. Search related indicators across the authorized customer scope if needed. Determine whether the same file or activity appears elsewhere.
  6. Record your finding and the response result, and coordinate with the MDR provider or incident owner before duplicating actions.

Know what the response buttons affect

ActionWhat to confirm
Kill processStops the selected malicious process or supported threat-related processes. Does not by itself prove all persistence was removed.
Quarantine fileMakes the identified file unavailable for normal use. Check the action result and exactly which artifact was affected.
Network isolation / disconnectRestricts the endpoint’s network communication, with management exceptions depending on the product. Can disrupt user work and remote support.
Remediate / RollbackSupported cleanup or recovery actions. Availability and recovery coverage vary; rollback is not a substitute for backups.
Resolve / mark benignUpdates the investigation classification or workflow. Closing an alert is not proof that the underlying device was cleaned.

Practice reading a Storyline

Fictional activity
09:41  outlook.exe opens an attachment
09:42  attachment starts powershell.exe
09:42  powershell.exe downloads a new executable
09:43  SentinelOne reports a detection; process termination succeeds

The useful question is whether the behavior matches a legitimate workflow, and what happened before termination. Check the downloaded file, network destination, additional child processes, user context, and any later activity. “The process was killed” answers one part of the investigation, not whether account credentials or other devices were affected.

Useful ticket evidence

Capture the detection ID, endpoint and customer, relevant Storyline details, indicators, timestamps with time zone, completed and failed actions, and the current owner. If the agent is offline, record its last contact and verify the device’s actual state before assuming a queued action has happened.
articles.question: A threat says “resolved,” but the endpoint has been offline since before isolation was requested. What do you verify?
articles.answer: Verify the isolation action’s result and the device’s current connectivity, not just the alert’s workflow status. Check last contact and pending or failed actions. Coordinate the next containment step with the incident owner and document the uncertainty.
articles.keywords: Storyline Deep Visibility quarantine isolate EDR

articles.title: Blackpoint
articles.principle: Blackpoint’s CompassOne platform gives a customer team visibility into protected assets, security findings, and the work performed by Blackpoint’s response service.
articles.body:
Use this as a guide to reviewing the service and its evidence. General MDR concepts are in EDR, MDR, and XDR. CompassOne capabilities and labels depend on the customer’s enabled services and permissions; use the current partner documentation for exact click paths.

What to look for in the platform

Area of workWhat you need to establish
Customer / tenant contextThe organization whose data and actions you are viewing. MSPs support multiple customers.
Asset inventoryWhich endpoints are present and covered, and whether their information is current.
Detection and response findingsThe affected entities, evidence, urgency, response already performed, and outstanding recommendations.
IntegrationsWhich services are connected and healthy, including SentinelOne when configured.
Cloud posture and identity findingsThe relevant Microsoft 365 or identity coverage when those services are enabled.
ReportingThe record of findings and actions that supports customer follow-up.

Review a SentinelOne-related escalation

Blackpoint documents an integration that monitors SentinelOne alerts, investigates them, performs supported response, and adds resolution notes back in SentinelOne. Start by reading those notes. If the provider already terminated a process or isolated an endpoint, confirm the outcome and coordinate remaining work instead of repeating the action blindly.

  1. Match the Blackpoint finding to the customer, device, and SentinelOne detection ID.
  2. Read the timeline: what was observed, what was judged malicious, and what the SOC already did.
  3. Identify remaining tasks such as checking an account, patching software, restoring a device, or communicating with the customer.
  4. Confirm who owns each task and when restoration is allowed.
  5. Record your validation in the customer’s incident or service ticket.

Separate service status from recovery

In a fictional case, Blackpoint reports that a malicious process was stopped on FIN-LT-07. Your remaining work may include confirming the affected employee can use a replacement device, checking related account activity, and arranging remediation with the incident owner. The provider’s completed containment does not automatically mean the user’s business service is restored.

Before closing the customer ticket, verify the required remediation and monitoring are complete. Before releasing isolation, check the recovery criteria agreed by the incident owner. Preserve the provider’s findings and your own validation so the next analyst can see why the decision was made.

Check coverage before assuming visibility

A platform can only analyze data its sensors and integrations supply. Confirm that a device is onboarded, an integration is healthy, and the relevant service is included. Do not assume that “Blackpoint” means every firewall, mailbox, cloud application, and endpoint is automatically visible.

Questions worth asking the service owner

Which customers and devices are covered? Which integrations are enabled? Which actions can the provider take immediately? Who handles the customer’s recovery and communication? These answers make an escalation actionable.
articles.question: Blackpoint reports successful containment. Why might the customer ticket still need work?
articles.answer: Containment stops or limits the threat. The customer may still need remediation, account investigation, service recovery, and communication. Read the provider’s evidence, confirm the action outcome, and assign the remaining work before closing the ticket.

articles.title: SIEM
articles.principle: A SIEM collects searchable security data from different systems and applies detection rules. It helps an analyst investigate a sequence of events across the environment.
articles.body:
Why collect logs together?

A firewall can show a blocked connection. A Windows server can show a failed logon. An email system can show message delivery. Opening each device separately is slow, especially across many customers. A Security Information and Event Management platform brings configured sources into a place where you can search and compare them. Microsoft Sentinel is one example.

Follow the data

  1. Generate: a source system records an event.
  2. Collect: an agent, API connector, or log forwarder sends it.
  3. Parse: fields such as timestamp, account, IP, and action become searchable. Some connectors also normalize different vendor formats into common fields.
  4. Detect: a rule evaluates the data, for example many failed logons followed by a success.
  5. Investigate: an analyst examines the alert and related evidence. Several related alerts may be grouped into an incident.

An event records something that happened. An alert flags activity that matched detection logic. An incident is a unit of investigation that can group related alerts and entities. These are not interchangeable.

Work through a simple case

Imagine 30 failed logons against one server, followed by a successful logon from the same source. A detection rule might raise an alert. The analyst asks whether the account normally signs in that way, what kind of logon succeeded, and what happened afterward. The pattern could indicate password guessing, but it could also involve a broken service followed by a legitimate user. The raw events and context support the conclusion.

A rule must define its time window, grouping, exclusions, and threshold. Thirty failures against one user are a different question from thirty failures spread across many users. Tuning is the process of adjusting detection logic to make it useful while preserving visibility.

What a dashboard cannot prove

  • No alert does not prove no attack occurred. Data may be missing, a rule may not cover the behavior, or a threshold may not be reached.
  • A map based on an IP address estimates the address’s location. It does not identify the attacker’s physical location.
  • A colorful dashboard is a view of data. Verify source health, timestamps, and fields before trusting its interpretation.
  • Central collection does not automatically grant response authority. Automated actions need configured permissions and an approved workflow.

Use it during daily review

Check the incident queue and source health. For an investigation, select the correct customer or workspace, define a time range, and search the account, device, or IP. Record relevant results and the query that produced them. Compare endpoint and identity evidence where available. Escalate with a concise timeline, impact, actions already taken, and the next decision needed.
articles.question: How can a SIEM contain logs without producing an alert about those logs?
articles.answer: Collection and detection are separate. The source may be sending events successfully while no enabled rule matches the behavior, its threshold is not reached, or its query looks in the wrong table or time range. Check the raw events before changing the detection.

articles.title: Microsoft Sentinel
articles.principle: Microsoft Sentinel lets you connect security data, query it with KQL, investigate incidents, and build workbooks and detection rules around the connected data.
articles.body:
This guide focuses on the product and the Windows-event collection path used in the study lab. For the general role of this type of platform, read SIEM. Microsoft Sentinel and SentinelOne are separate products.

Find the feature you need

In the Defender portal, Sentinel features sit alongside the unified incident and hunting experience. Older lab material may use the Azure portal. The table below follows Microsoft’s current navigation reference; menus and access can vary with the workspace, role, and enabled services.

TaskDefender portal location
Review incidentsInvestigation & response → Incidents & alerts → Incidents
Run queriesInvestigation & response → Hunting → Advanced hunting
Find integrationsMicrosoft Sentinel → Configuration → Data connectors
Review detection rulesMicrosoft Sentinel → Configuration → Analytics
Use workbook dashboardsMicrosoft Sentinel → Threat management → Workbooks
Add solution contentMicrosoft Sentinel → Content management → Content hub
Maintain lookup dataMicrosoft Sentinel → Configuration → Watchlists

Know the pieces in the Windows lab

ComponentIts job in this collection path
Event ViewerShows events recorded on the Windows machine itself. Useful for confirming an event exists before troubleshooting collection.
Azure Monitor Agent (AMA)Collects the configured events from the machine.
Data Collection Rule (DCR)Specifies what to collect and where to send it; the machine must be associated with the rule.
Log Analytics workspaceStores the collected records in tables. The Windows Security Events via AMA connector uses SecurityEvent.
SentinelUses the connected data for queries, detections, incidents, and visualizations.

Run a first query

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventID == 4625
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, IpAddress
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 50

This selects up to 50 recent failed-logon records. It requires access to the appropriate workspace and a populated SecurityEvent table. It is a log query, not automatically an alert. Column names and tables in other connectors can differ.

When a query returns nothing

  1. Check the correct machine’s Event Viewer for a known event and timestamp.
  2. Check agent health and the machine’s DCR association.
  3. Confirm the DCR selects the necessary Security events and destination workspace.
  4. Check the table, workspace access, time range, ingestion delay, and query filters.
  5. Test with a small query before rebuilding a workbook or detection rule.

Review an incident

Confirm its status, owner, time range, associated alerts, and affected entities. Inspect the underlying events and record the timeline and response. A workbook is a visualization; an analytics rule defines detection logic. Updating a workbook does not fix an unrelated analytics rule.

Lab troubleshooting lesson

When a workbook expects a watchlist but the data source changes, update the workbook’s own query too. Inaccessible portal navigation and a missing query column are separate problems. Check workspace onboarding and permissions for the first; inspect the data schema for the second.
articles.question: A known failed logon exists in Event Viewer but is absent from Sentinel. What would you check next?
articles.answer: Check AMA health, the machine’s DCR association, the selected event collection, and the destination workspace. Then verify SecurityEvent, your access, the time range, and ingestion delay. The local event confirms generation; it does not prove collection succeeded.
articles.keywords: Sentinel AMA DCR LAW Log Analytics

articles.title: Timus
articles.principle: Timus Manager is the web console for administering users, devices, sites, and access policies. Timus Connect is the client application employees use to connect through the configured service.
articles.body:
This is a product cheat sheet. The general access model and the comparison with a VPN or virtual desktop are covered in ZTNA / SASE. Timus does not provide a Windows desktop for the user to log into like a Citrix virtual desktop session.

Recognize the two interfaces

InterfaceWhat happens there
Timus ManagerAdministrators manage the customer’s configuration, users, teams, devices, sites, policies, integrations, and logs.
Timus ConnectAn employee signs in and connects from the endpoint using the configuration assigned to them.
User portalUsers can obtain the client through the available downloads workflow. Administrators also have downloads in Manager.

Find the setting behind the symptom

Manager areaWhat to inspect
Users / TeamsThe correct user record and team membership. Compare with a working user who should have equivalent access.
Devices / Agent ProfilesThe device record and the profile or requirements that apply to it.
Sites / NetworksThe intended gateway, network, and connection configuration.
Firewall Rules / access policiesThe source user or team, destination, service, conditions, and matching decision.
Settings → IntegrationsThe configured identity provider and supported security integrations.
Settings → Administrators → Audit LogsWho changed an administrative setting and when.
Settings → Administrators → Roles & PermissionsWhich management tasks the administrator is allowed to perform.

Exact labels and available features can change by release and plan. Use the linked setup guide and your organization’s configuration record when following a specific screen path.

Work a “connected, but file share fails” ticket

  1. Record the customer, user, device, requested server name, service, error, and time. “Connected” is only one status.
  2. Confirm Timus Connect is signed in as the expected user and connected to the intended site.
  3. Inspect the matching user, team, device, and assigned profile in Manager.
  4. Check the relevant access or traffic event. Identify the actual denied condition or rule rather than assuming it is a password problem.
  5. Verify name resolution and the destination’s availability. Compare the case with a working user or device that should have the same access.
  6. If a change is required, apply it within the approved scope and retest the same resource. Document the rule, result, and any remaining server-side permission issue.

Read a denial usefully

For a fictional finance employee, a denial might involve the wrong team, an unmet device requirement, a destination excluded by policy, or a missing path to a site. Those require different corrections. Record the reason shown by the product. A successful connection to one application does not prove all destinations are allowed.

Keep management and user problems separate

An administrator lacking permission to edit a rule is different from an employee being denied access to a server. Check the administrator role for the first and the employee’s policy and traffic path for the second. If the client is not connecting, use the current Timus troubleshooting guidance and diagnostic logs before changing access policy.
articles.question: An employee is connected in Timus Connect but cannot use one internal application. What details make the ticket actionable?
articles.answer: Record the customer, signed-in user, device, site, application hostname, destination port, time, and error. Review the matching policy decision, team and profile, then check DNS and the destination service. Connection status alone does not show that this application is permitted.

articles.title: ZTNA / SASE
articles.principle: ZTNA checks who is requesting access and the conditions of that request before allowing a path to a resource. SASE combines secure access with wider networking and security services.
articles.body:
Start with a remote employee

An employee at home needs a company finance application. That application might be on a private office server, so an ordinary internet connection is not enough. Zero Trust Network Access provides an approved path based on identity, the requested resource, and configured context such as device status.

A resource can be an internal web application or another supported private service. The employee may use a local client or a browser, depending on the product and application. They do not necessarily open a virtual Windows desktop. The goal is to grant the required access with the conditions the organization has chosen.

Walk through an access request

  1. The employee signs in using the organization’s identity provider.
  2. The service evaluates the applicable access policy: user or group, resource, and relevant device or risk conditions.
  3. If requirements are met, the system provides the permitted connection to that resource.
  4. The application still checks its own sign-in and permissions. Network access does not automatically grant access to every file.
  5. Access can be reevaluated when supported signals or sessions change. The exact timing and behavior depend on the implementation.

Compare the experiences

ApproachWhat the employee experiences
VPNA tunnel provides access to configured network routes. Its reach can be broad or tightly restricted; a VPN does not inherently grant every permission.
ZTNAAccess is granted according to identity, resource, and policy context. Supported protocols and the granularity of controls depend on the product.
Virtual desktop, such as a Citrix desktopThe employee operates a remote desktop or published application. Much of the work runs on the remote system rather than directly on the local laptop.

A personal computer is not universally allowed or forbidden by ZTNA. The organization may require a managed device, allow limited browser access, or use another design. Likewise, “always on” describes how a configured client maintains protection; it does not mean every resource is available to every signed-in user.

Where SASE fits

Secure Access Service Edge, commonly pronounced “sassy,” is the broader architecture. It combines networking, such as software-defined wide area networking (SD-WAN), with cloud-delivered security. Common parts include ZTNA, web filtering through a secure web gateway, controls for cloud application use through a CASB, and firewall-as-a-service. A product may deliver a subset; verify the deployed capabilities.

Use it on a support ticket

For “I can sign in but cannot reach the app,” separate identity, policy, network path, and application permissions. A successful MFA challenge confirms one requirement, not every requirement. Check the request’s policy result, device state, DNS, connector or gateway health, and the resource itself. A precise denial reason is more useful than turning off a policy to make the error disappear.

Conditional Access is one part of the picture

A sign-in policy can require MFA or a compliant device for an application. By itself, that policy does not create a network path from a home laptop to a private file server. The access service and the application’s own permissions still matter.
articles.question: Why does successful MFA not guarantee that an employee can open a private file share?
articles.answer: MFA satisfies an authentication requirement. The device and request must also meet the access policy, the private server must be reachable through an approved path, and the user must have permission on the share and files.

articles.title: Email authentication
articles.principle: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC help check whether a message is authorized to use a domain. They do not prove that the sender is honest or that the request is safe.
articles.body:
Start with the visible sender

An email contains several sender-related fields. The display name is the friendly label, such as “Finance Director.” The From address is what the mail client displays. The envelope sender is used during delivery and can differ from that visible From address. Authentication checks these identities in specific ways; a convincing display name proves very little.

What each check means

CheckPlain-English questionLimit
SPF — Sender Policy FrameworkIs this sending server authorized in DNS to send for the envelope-sender domain?An SPF pass alone does not authenticate the visible From domain. Forwarding can complicate SPF.
DKIM — DomainKeys Identified MailDoes a valid signature from the signing domain verify the signed parts of this message?It checks signed content and domain responsibility, not the truth of the message or every possible header.
DMARC — Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and ConformanceDid SPF or DKIM pass with a domain that aligns with the visible From domain?A passing message can still be fraudulent. A failing result needs delivery-path context.

DMARC needs at least one aligned passing method, not both. Alignment means the authenticated domain matches the visible From domain according to the configured strict or relaxed rules. Relaxed alignment can allow related subdomains of the same organizational domain.

Compare three messages

Fictional caseWhat the checks can tell you
Forged From: finance@company.example, sent through an unauthorized systemDMARC can fail because neither SPF nor DKIM passes with alignment to company.example.
From: finance@company-payments.example, a lookalike domain owned by an attackerSPF, DKIM, and DMARC can all pass for the attacker’s own domain. The domain still is not company.example.
A real employee mailbox has been compromisedMessages sent through the legitimate service can authenticate successfully while carrying fraudulent instructions.

Read it during phishing review

Use your email security platform or the original message headers to inspect the receiving system’s authentication results. Compare the actual From address, Reply-To, envelope sender, DKIM signing domain, and links with the organization the sender claims to represent. A raw authentication-looking header supplied by an untrusted sender is not automatically trustworthy; use the results from your trusted receiving system.

Then inspect the request itself. Was a bank account changed? Is the message pressuring the user to bypass a normal process? Did the recipient click, download, enter credentials, or approve MFA? Search for other recipients and related activity through the available email tools.

Understand the policy

A domain’s DMARC policy can request monitoring only (p=none), quarantine, or rejection of failing mail. Receiver handling also depends on the receiving system’s policies. Publishing a monitoring policy is not the same as enforcing rejection.
articles.question: Why can a lookalike domain pass DMARC?
articles.answer: The attacker can configure valid SPF and DKIM for the domain they own, aligned with that domain’s From address. DMARC checks domain authorization, not whether the domain is the real company or whether the payment request is legitimate.

articles.title: Business email compromise
articles.principle: Business email compromise is a scam that uses a believable business conversation to trick someone into sending money, sharing information, or changing an important process.
articles.body:
Recognize the attack

A message appears to come from a supplier: “Our bank details changed; please use this account.” It may contain no malware and no suspicious attachment. The attacker wants the employee to perform the harmful action willingly. BEC is an attack scenario, not an email security framework.

The message might use a forged sender, a similar-looking domain, or an actual compromised mailbox. Attackers can reply inside an existing conversation and copy its tone. A familiar name, a real signature, and passing email authentication do not establish that a new payment instruction is legitimate.

Start with the requested action and exposure

  1. Ask the recipient to pause the requested action and avoid further interaction with the suspicious message.
  2. Determine what already happened: reply, click, download, credential entry, MFA approval, data disclosure, or payment.
  3. Preserve the original message and useful identifiers, headers, timestamps, and relevant conversation history.
  4. Verify the business request through a known independent contact method, such as a number already in approved supplier records. Do not use new contact details supplied by the suspect message.

Investigate more than the header

Inspect the sender domains, Reply-To, authentication results, links, and message delivery. Search for other recipients and related messages. If a mailbox may be compromised, examine sign-ins, mailbox rules, forwarding, sent messages, permission changes, and other relevant audit activity with the tools available. Distinguish what is observed from what is still suspected.

SPF, DKIM, and DMARC help evaluate domain use. They do not clear a legitimate but compromised account or a well-configured lookalike domain. The authenticity of a payment change still needs independent business verification.

Match the response to what happened

ExposureTypical response work within the incident plan
Message received, no interactionEvaluate and scope the message; remove or quarantine confirmed malicious copies as authorized and explain the finding to the user.
Credentials entered or suspicious MFA approvedCoordinate account containment, credential and session response, authentication-method review, and investigation of account activity.
Attachment executedInvestigate the endpoint and consider immediate containment using the available evidence and authority.
Payment or sensitive data already sentEscalate immediately through the organization’s incident and business response process. For payment fraud, the responsible team should promptly contact its financial institution.

Make the handoff useful

Record the claimed sender, actual domain, recipients, actions the user took, evidence, affected accounts or devices, containment already completed, and the owner of each next step. A high-impact event may need containment and escalation while further confirmation continues. Avoid a rule such as “always wait until completely certain” that could delay an urgent response.
articles.question: A supplier’s email passes DMARC and asks for new bank details. Is it safe to approve the change?
articles.answer: No. A compromised supplier mailbox or a lookalike domain can pass authentication. Pause the change, verify it through an existing trusted contact method, and investigate the message and any user interaction. Escalate promptly if money or sensitive information has already been sent.

articles.title: Risky sign-ins
articles.principle: A risky sign-in is an authentication event with signals that deserve investigation. The signal helps prioritize work; the surrounding evidence determines whether an account is compromised.
articles.body:
Understand the signal

An account signs in from Colorado and soon afterward appears to sign in from another continent. That travel seems implausible, so an identity system may flag it. An impossible-travel style detection compares time and apparent locations; other signals include unfamiliar properties or known malicious infrastructure. Names and logic vary by provider.

A network location is normally inferred from the IP address. A VPN, mobile provider, cloud proxy, or inaccurate location database can change that appearance without the user physically moving. Conversely, a familiar location is not proof of safety. Attackers may use nearby infrastructure or an already-established session.

Read the sign-in as a record

FieldWhy it matters
User and tenantIdentify the actual account and organization. Similar display names can mislead.
Time and resultEstablish whether authentication succeeded and keep the time zone consistent.
Application / resourceIdentify what the account was trying to access.
IP, device, client, and locationCompare with the account’s usual pattern and known company infrastructure.
Authentication detailsSee how MFA or another requirement was satisfied; a success can rely on an earlier claim or session.
Conditional Access resultIdentify which policies applied, which requirement failed, or why access was allowed.

Work through the investigation

  1. Confirm the alert’s evidence and whether suspicious access succeeded. Compare nearby sign-ins, devices, and expected VPN use.
  2. Contact the user through a trusted channel to verify relevant activity, without relying only on their recollection.
  3. Look for subsequent resource activity: mailbox rules, sent messages, downloaded files, changed authentication methods, or new permissions where logs are available.
  4. Assess impact and urgency. Use the incident plan to contain credible active compromise while continuing investigation.
  5. Document the evidence, alternative explanations, actions, and the remaining uncertainty.

Containment is more than a password reset

Authorized response can include blocking sign-in, resetting credentials, revoking sessions, and reviewing registered authentication methods or suspicious application access. These actions have different effects. Revocation is not a promise that every existing token or application session immediately becomes unusable; token lifetime, application behavior, and supported continuous evaluation matter. Verify the observed outcome.

Do not delete every authentication method automatically because a location looked unusual. Determine what was changed or abused and use the approved recovery procedure. Similarly, changing a password does not remove a malicious forwarding rule or identify which data was accessed.

Use the right source of evidence

Entra sign-in logs explain authentication. Email and cloud application audit records show relevant activity within those services. Endpoint tools show device activity. Intune provides device-management and compliance information; it is not a universal record of everything an attacker did.
articles.question: Two successful sign-ins appear far apart within minutes. What would make you more or less concerned?
articles.answer: Compare known VPN or proxy use, device and client details, authentication and policy results, and subsequent activity. A user-confirmed VPN with expected behavior may explain the location shift. Unexpected MFA changes, mailbox forwarding, or unfamiliar resource access increase concern and may justify prompt containment under the response plan.

articles.title: Active Directory
articles.principle: Active Directory Domain Services keeps a shared directory of users, computers, and groups. Domain controllers use it to support domain authentication and centralized administration.
articles.body:
Server, role, and domain controller

Windows Server is an operating system. Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) is a role it can run. A server promoted to run AD DS as a domain controller maintains the directory and provides domain services. A file server can run Windows Server without being a domain controller.

A domain is a directory and administration boundary containing objects such as user accounts and computers. A group collects identities so permissions can be assigned together. An organizational unit (OU) is a container used to organize objects, delegate administration, and apply Group Policy. An OU is not a permission group.

Follow an ordinary domain sign-in

  1. A domain-joined PC has a relationship with the domain. It uses DNS to locate appropriate domain services.
  2. During a typical connected domain sign-in, Windows communicates with a domain controller to authenticate the user. Kerberos is commonly used.
  3. Kerberos provides tickets the user can use to request access to supported services without sending the password to every server.
  4. The destination service checks authorization, including group membership and its own permissions. A successful logon does not grant access to all files.

Windows can permit cached interactive sign-in when a domain controller is unavailable, depending on configuration and prior sign-ins. Reaching the desktop therefore does not prove the PC can currently contact a domain controller or obtain access to a network resource.

What Group Policy does

Administrators use Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to apply settings to users and computers, such as password-related configuration, firewall settings, or drive mappings. Where a GPO is linked, its filtering, inheritance, and processing determine who receives it. Changing a domain-wide GPO can affect many systems.

Troubleshoot from the symptom

SymptomUseful checks
One user cannot sign inExact error, correct domain, account enabled or locked, password status, and relevant log events.
Many devices cannot use domain servicesDNS configuration, domain controller reachability, service health, and recent changes.
Desktop sign-in works but a share failsNetwork path, current domain connectivity, user identity, group membership, and share/file permissions.
Expected policy is missingApplied-policy results, object location, links and filtering, and domain connectivity.

Keep AD DS and Entra ID distinct

Microsoft Entra ID, formerly Azure AD, is Microsoft’s cloud identity service. It is not simply an on-premises domain controller with a new name. Organizations can synchronize selected identities between AD DS and Entra ID, so a user may appear in both. Identify whether the problem concerns a local account, domain account, cloud sign-in, or synchronization before choosing a console or reset procedure.
articles.question: Does every Windows Server machine validate domain logons?
articles.answer: No. Windows Server can host many roles. Domain controllers running AD DS provide domain authentication services. A server used only for file sharing or an application is not automatically a domain controller.

articles.title: Windows Server
articles.principle: Windows Server is Microsoft’s operating system for shared services such as domains, DNS, DHCP, files, and applications. Start by identifying the role a server performs and who depends on it.
articles.body:
What makes it a server?

A server provides a service to other computers. It can be a physical machine or a virtual machine. Windows Server supplies the operating system and optional roles. One machine might host several roles, but the roles are separate responsibilities. A domain controller is one possible configuration, not another name for every Windows Server.

These are starting points for supporting Windows Server 2019 and newer systems. Some installations use a graphical desktop; Server Core installations rely more on command-line and remote administration. Available consoles depend on the installed roles and management tools.

Find your way around

ToolWhat to use it for
Server ManagerInspect the server, installed roles, and role-related tools. Confirm the machine and role before making a change.
Event ViewerRead System, Application, and relevant Security logs. Filter by time and event ID; open details rather than relying only on the short message.
ServicesCheck whether a required service is running and its startup configuration. A restart can affect every dependent user.
Task Manager / performance toolsCheck CPU, memory, disk, and process pressure when a service is slow.
DNS / DHCP consolesInspect records, zones, scopes, leases, and options when the corresponding role is installed.
AD Users and Computers / Group Policy ManagementAdminister domain objects and policy with the appropriate permissions and installed tools.
Windows Admin Center / PowerShellManage systems remotely and collect repeatable diagnostic information.

Useful read-only starting checks

hostname
ipconfig /all
Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq "Stopped"
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName="System"; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddHours(-2)} -MaxEvents 30
Get-Volume

Run these in a suitable Windows PowerShell session on the intended server with authorized access. They identify the host and networking, list stopped services, read recent System events, and show volume state. Many services are normally stopped: compare against the role’s requirements, not a rule that every service must run.

Work a “shared folder is unavailable” ticket

  1. Establish scope: one user, one department, or everyone? Record the exact path and error.
  2. Identify which server provides that share and whether it is reachable by its expected name.
  3. Check the relevant service, recent events, free disk space, and any recent patch or configuration change.
  4. If the share is reachable but access is denied, inspect the user’s identity and effective permissions.
  5. Escalate with the server role, impact, time, checks, and evidence before a disruptive restart or broad permission change.

Daily habits that matter

Review service health, security events, patch state, backup status, storage capacity, and monitoring alerts according to the customer’s procedures. A successful backup job does not replace a tested restore plan. Check the impact and approved maintenance process before restarting a server: the laptop you are using is only one of many possible clients.
articles.question: A service is stopped in Services. Does that prove it caused the outage?
articles.answer: No. Some services normally start only when needed or are not used by this server’s role. Compare the affected function with its dependencies, configured startup behavior, recent events, and a known-good baseline before changing the service.

articles.title: File shares
articles.principle: A file share lets other computers access a folder over the network. The network path finds the server and share; the user’s permissions decide what they can do there.
articles.body:
Read the path

\\files-01\Finance
Z:  →  \\files-01\Finance

A path beginning with two backslashes is a UNC path. files-01 is the server name and Finance is the share name. A mapped drive such as Z: is a convenient local shortcut to that path. Losing the drive letter does not necessarily mean the files or server disappeared.

A file server can be a general-purpose server offering folders. A NAS, or network-attached storage device, is a storage-focused appliance that can also offer shares. Both may provide SMB, the file-sharing protocol commonly used by Windows. Modern direct SMB commonly uses TCP port 445.

Four things must work

  1. Name: the computer resolves the server name to the intended address.
  2. Path: the network and any approved remote-access service can reach the server’s SMB service.
  3. Identity: the server authenticates the account being used.
  4. Permission: the account is authorized to use the share and the requested files.

Being on the same network or connected through a VPN does not expose every person’s files automatically. A folder must be shared and permissions must allow the requested access. The same applies when an access service permits the network connection.

Share permissions and file permissions

Windows file access over a share is constrained by both the share’s permissions and the file system’s permissions, commonly NTFS permissions. Allowing Modify on the share does not override a file permission that prevents the write. Use effective-access tools and the actual group memberships when troubleshooting; inherited permissions and deny entries can make a quick glance misleading.

Troubleshoot a missing mapped drive

  1. Record the drive letter, expected UNC path, user, error, and whether other users are affected.
  2. Try the known UNC path. If it works, investigate the mapping or its deployment policy.
  3. If the name fails, check DNS and the remote-access path. A service-port test can help separate reachability from authorization.
  4. If the share opens but writing fails, check the exact account, share permissions, file permissions, and storage state.
  5. If everyone is affected, inspect server and service health, disk space, and recent changes.
Resolve-DnsName files-01
Test-NetConnection files-01 -Port 445
Get-SmbMapping

These Windows checks inspect name resolution, a TCP connection, and existing drive mappings. Substitute the actual server. A successful TCP check does not prove the user can authenticate or read a folder. Avoid granting broad access as a shortcut; restore the intended access for the affected group.
articles.question: Z: disappeared, but the expected UNC path opens successfully. What is your next focus?
articles.answer: The server path and this user’s basic access work. Investigate the drive mapping, sign-in script, Group Policy, or device-management configuration that should create Z:. Also check whether the problem is limited to one session or device.

articles.title: Microsoft 365
articles.principle: Microsoft 365 combines work applications with identity, device management, and security services. Entra identifies users, Intune manages devices, Defender investigates threats, and Conditional Access controls sign-ins.
articles.body:
Start with the employee’s workday

An employee opens Outlook, joins a Teams call, and edits a file in SharePoint. Those familiar applications rely on several systems underneath. Exchange Online hosts cloud email. SharePoint and OneDrive provide collaboration and file storage. Teams provides collaboration and uses other Microsoft 365 services for parts of its experience. The organization’s tenant is its instance of these cloud services.

Know which service answers which question

ServiceQuestion it helps answerCommon analyst use
Microsoft Entra IDWho is the user and how did they sign in?Review users, groups, sign-in logs, authentication methods, and risk where available. Azure AD is its former name.
Conditional AccessUnder what conditions may this user access this application?Inspect the actual policy result and requirements such as MFA or a compliant device. This is an Entra capability.
Microsoft IntuneHow is this device managed, configured, and evaluated?Check enrollment, last check-in, compliance findings, configuration, and app deployment.
Microsoft DefenderWhat threats or suspicious activity are detected?Investigate endpoint, email, identity, or cloud application evidence in the relevant Defender service.
Microsoft 365 admin centerIs a service, account, or license affecting the employee?Check service health, users, and licensed services before treating every outage as a security incident.

“Defender” is a family of products

Defender for Endpoint supplies endpoint investigation and response. Defender for Office 365 focuses on threats involving email and collaboration. Defender for Identity provides signals about supported identity environments, including AD DS. Defender for Cloud Apps provides cloud application security capabilities. Defender XDR connects signals from enabled products into investigations. A customer does not automatically have every component or feature.

INTERACTIVE / FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Make an access decision

Try a SharePoint request: Conditional Access requires MFA and a compliant device; the files separately require Finance group membership. Change a signal and follow both decisions.

How the services work together
